input.purpose: Measure V_lab, the air volume served by /habitat/lab/eclss/scrubber-1-v1, from the CO2 rise-and-decay time constant and the scrubber effective flow.
hypotheses: The Lab behaves as one well-mixed zone during both phases.

The closed hatch exchange between /habitat/lab and /habitat/hab-b is unmeasured and small or stable enough not to dominate the fitted Lab decay; the Hab-B CO2 record is used to detect contrary evidence.
The same four occupants remain in the Lab at steady activity throughout the test, so their aggregate CO2 source is approximately steady.

The scrubber effective flow at each accepted speed is given by its commissioned device characteristic; V_lab is calculated as effective flow at full speed multiplied by the fitted decay time constant.
The decay is fitted to C(t) = C_eq + (C_0 - C_eq) exp(-t/tau), not to zero or outdoor concentration.

monitoring.reason: The test deliberately raises CO2 in occupied air; stop for an out-of-band vital sign, monitoring loss, or occupancy change.

steps.why: Hold the Lab as one zone and reduce effective scrubbing so occupant-generated CO2 rises several hundred ppm above sensor noise; record both module CO2 sensors, accepted speed, and occupancy at one-minute intervals.
Keep the opening position and source unchanged, restore full speed, and record the decay at one-minute intervals for an equilibrium-offset exponential fit.

abort.when: Lab CO2 reaches or exceeds 3200 ppm.
The scrubber refuses either commanded speed.
Battery state of charge is below 35 percent.
Any monitored subject leaves the 45–120 bpm band, monitoring is lost, or anyone enters or leaves the Lab.

expected.baseline: Begin from the observed Lab CO2 concentration of 800 ppm and verify the hatch is closed, all four named occupants remain present at steady activity, and both module CO2 sensors are recording once per minute.
expected.rise: At 30 percent speed, Lab CO2 should rise by several hundred ppm while remaining below 3000 ppm. Failure to rise above noise indicates inadequate excitation or a source/flow assumption failure.
expected.decay: At 100 percent speed, Lab CO2 should decay toward a nonzero fitted equilibrium. Fit C(t) = C_eq + (C_0 - C_eq) exp(-t/tau), then compute V_lab = Qe,full × tau using the scrubber's registered effective full-speed flow.
expected.opening_check: Hab-B CO2 should not track the Lab transient strongly with the hatch closed. A correlated transient indicates material inter-zone exchange and rejects the single-zone/low-exchange hypothesis.
expected.validity: A speed refusal, occupancy change, non-steady activity, vital alarm, monitoring loss, CO2 abort, battery abort, or poor exponential fit invalidates the volume result; do not infer V_lab from that run.
